reads_as_reason: Smooth and clean, but the thigh is a near-parallel slab and the knee is a bare slit with a raw flat cut face on the shank: a molded blank, not a finished shell.

G1.evidence: Thigh is an almost parallel-sided slab-like bar with small corner radii; nothing reads as designed product surface. P8a 0.708 and P8b 0.712 fail.

G2.evidence: Thigh-to-shank is a thin slit in the side view; the back view shows a flat D-shaped planar cut face; 65 and 130 degree views show a raw diagonal chop. Flow inside each segment is good (S3a 0).

G3.evidence: No colour; only a hairline gap at the knee.

G4.evidence: Similar end radii and squareness; the sharp planar cut at the shank top breaks the radius family.

G6.evidence: No references. Rounded-rectangle section and knee bulge loosely similar; no clear taper, calf swell or knee mass.

pairwise.evidence: Both sheets share the same target silhouette and near-identical outlines, so the difference is surface quality. The candidate has smooth concentric contour lines and clean continuous zebra bands; the baseline has noisy blotchy zebra, facet-like contour kinks on the shank and a chamfered polygonal shank bottom. Modest preference: the main weaknesses are shared.

top_changes.change: Real thigh taper: narrow the distal section in width and depth (P8a).
Crown flat faces (lower n at mid-thigh and calf) and deepen the calf-to-ankle taper (S4a, P8b).
Remove the raw planar cut at the shank top; soften the proximal edge, widen the knee gap slightly.

notes: Round 2. Chunkiness caused by the 35 mm servos was not counted against the design.
